A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rc-BT research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are readable and support comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model and DPO experiments, length-bias diagnostics, component ablations, and HH-RLHF transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds PPO results, human evaluation of dataset labels, augmentation-quantity experiments, and format-bias evaluation.

M1.justification: Appendix E.6 adds a format-specific adaptation of response-conditioned training-pair construction using formatting constraints and correct/incorrect options. The original length-based Rc-BT construction, reward-model architecture, and Rc-RM/Rc-DPO objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on FormatBiasEval multiple-choice questions with formatting requirements, extending coverage beyond length bias to output-format bias. OpenAssistant, HH-RLHF, AlpacaEval, and both length-instruction variants remain.

E2.justification: The six-model RM comparison drops LIFT-plus from quality accuracy and ODIN from length accuracy when v1 Table 1 becomes v2 Tables 3 and 8. Both methods remain in other comparisons. v2 also evaluates Pc-Format in the new format experiment; the DPO comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include PPO training of a Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct policy with 1.5B/7B reward models, human validation involving 20 volunteers with ten sampled items each, and FormatBiasEval's predefined split with programmatically transformed evaluation pairs. v2 also sweeps total augmentation from 0% to 100%. Existing OpenAssistant splits and RM/DPO settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds accuracy analysis by chosen–rejected length difference, human validation of generated preference labels, and an ablation of total augmentation quantity. The latter is distinct from the retained experiment varying rejected-pair augmentation while holding chosen-pair augmentation fixed. Existing component, length-sensitivity, and transfer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing shaded plots retain their reporting practice; the new human-agreement percentage is a point estimate rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New results include PPO win ratios of 44.06% and 49.26% for Rc-RM versus 41.57% and 45.03% for ODIN (Table 4), 90.5% human agreement, and length-bin, augmentation-quantity, and format-bias results. Table 14 reports Rc-RM accuracies of 79.17%, 89.27%, and 84.24%. Matched retained tables preserve their values, while selected RM comparator entries are removed.

T1.justification: The Rc-BT objectives and Appendix B's complete Rc-DPO derivation remain mathematically unchanged. The LIFT expressions are regrouped and renumbered without changing their meaning; no new theorem, proof, or substantive theoretical argument is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that response-conditioned modeling mitigates length bias while preserving length-instruction following and applies to reward modeling and DPO. Explicitly naming Rc-RM in v2's abstract and emphasizing generalizability restate contributions already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds an augmentation-cost limitation, acknowledges GPT-4o's own length bias, and interprets new studies as supporting dataset validity, sample efficiency, and generalization across biases. The larger-model boundary was already acknowledged in v1. The new claim that 40% augmentation yields approximately 70% improvement is imprecise relative to Table 13.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies programmatic verification of response-length relationships, without establishing that the existing dataset was regenerated. Appendix E.6 documents format-data preparation and transformation steps. Conversely, v2 removes v1's statement that lambda is typically set to 1; PPO-specific training details remain sparse.

R1.justification: v2 adds Long et al. (2024) and connects the framework to output-format bias through FormatBiasEval. The existing RLHF, reward-hacking, and length-following literature and positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized around bias mitigation, moving length-following results into Appendix E and reordering supplementary subsections. Preliminary evidence moves into the main text. The conclusion is shortened, future-work discussion is replaced by a Limitations section, and numerous headings and explanatory passages are revised.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document, including converting most appendix prose to two columns. It splits v1 Table 1 into quality/length tables and Figure 2 into separate figures, relocates several displays, adds four experimental tables, expands the framework caption, and corrects Pc-RM legends to Rc-RM.

improvement.justification: Human label validation and downstream PPO evaluation strengthen confidence in the generated evaluation data and the usefulness of learned rewards beyond v1's standalone RM tests. Format-bias and augmentation studies add useful validation. These gains are limited by sparse PPO details, omitted comparator entries, and the imprecise efficiency interpretation accompanying Table 13.
